paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Joshua had just won a battle, and what does he do next? He doesn't throw a parade. He builds an altar and reads God's Word, because Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded it (Joshua 8:31). Victory is great, but the Word of God comes first, and that's the order I want in my bakery too.

Now look at HOW he does it. He builds it "according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses" (Joshua 8:31). He reads "all the words of the law—the blessings and the curses" (Joshua 8:34). And "There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua failed to read…" (Joshua 8:35). No skipping the easy parts, no skipping the hard parts. God's Word is meant to be taken whole, baker, not just the lines we like.

And who's standing there listening? "All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike" (Joshua 8:33), and the passage says the reading was before "the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them" (Joshua 8:35). Nobody was left outside the circle. God's Word is for everybody in the room, and that includes you, so pull up a chair and keep listening.
